content: The American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), pronounced ash-ray, is an international technical society that serves individuals and organizations interested in the fields of heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration (HVAC&R). The society is structured into regions, chapters, and student branches, which facilitate the exchange of knowledge and experiences in HVAC&R for the benefit of both practitioners and the public. ASHRAE provides numerous opportunities for members to contribute to the development of new knowledge, particularly through research and participation in its many Technical Committees. These committees typically convene twice a year during the ASHRAE Annual and Winter Meetings. Additionally, the Winter Meeting features a popular product exhibition known as the AHR Expo. The ASHRAE Handbook is a comprehensive four-volume resource on HVAC&R technology, available in both print and electronic formats. The four volumes are titled Fundamentals, HVAC Applications, HVAC Systems and Equipment, and Refrigeration. Each year, one of these volumes is updated. ASHRAE also publishes a widely recognized series of standards and guidelines related to HVAC systems and issues, which are frequently referenced in building codes. Notable examples include the Energy Standard for Buildings Except Low-Rise Residential Buildings and Standard 135 – BACnet: A Data Communication Protocol for Building Automation and Control Networks. These standards are periodically reviewed, revised, and republished, making the publication year critical for code compliance. ASHRAE publishes a monthly magazine called the ASHRAE Journal, which features peer-reviewed articles on the practical application of HVAC&R technology, information about upcoming meetings and product shows, classified and display advertisements, and editorials. Members of ASHRAE receive the magazine and the current year's volume of the ASHRAE Handbook as part of their membership benefits. The organization also produces numerous books, ASHRAE Transactions, and the International Journal of HVAC&R Research. ASHRAE was founded in 1894 during a meeting of like-minded engineers in New York City. Initially known as the American Society of Heating and Ventilating Engineers (ASHVE), it changed its name in 1954 to the American Society of Heating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHAE). The current name and organizational structure were established in 1959 following the merger of ASHAE with the American Society of Refrigerating Engineers (ASRE). Despite its name, ASHRAE is a globally influential organization with 55,000 members worldwide, all dedicated to advancing the arts and sciences of HVAC&R. The society's headquarters is located in Atlanta, Georgia, USA.
